source_batch.unit_label: BRBL::MOD_D::U03: Distinguish continuing exposure,revocation,death,variance and discharge

payload.title: Separate accrued liability from future transactions
payload.core_explanation_md:
A continuing guarantee extends to the described series of transactions. Revocation by notice ordinarily concerns future transactions; it does not automatically erase covered exposure already incurred. Death has the stated future-transaction effect absent contrary contract. The actual notice, knowledge, accounting and undertaking need careful reconciliation.

An unconsented variance and a contractual release of the principal debtor differ from mere forbearance to sue. Releasing one co-surety also has distinct consequences for other sureties and their contribution rights. Do not collapse every collection delay, renewal, settlement or death into the same complete-discharge result. Identify the event, consent, scope and timing before deciding what liability remains.

self_check.prompt_text: Does revocation necessarily remove covered debt already incurred?
self_check.expected_takeaway: No. Existing and future exposure must be separated.

payload.stem_md: A surety revokes a continuing guarantee after covered advances exist. Staff delete both those advances and every future exposure. Which distinction is needed?

options.text_md: Accrued covered liability differs from future transactions after effective revocation
options.explanation_md: Revocation does not automatically erase the earlier exposure.

options.text_md: A continuing guarantee can never be revoked
options.explanation_md: The source provides a future-transaction route.

options.text_md: The bank can invent consent to later changes

payload.correct_explanation_md: Revocation does not automatically erase the earlier exposure.

payload.stem_md: The creditor merely waits before suing, with no stipulated discharge agreement. Which comparison is appropriate?

options.text_md: Waiting and releasing the debtor always have identical effect
options.explanation_md: The source distinguishes forbearance from release.

options.text_md: Any delay automatically changes all guarantee terms
Mere forbearance is different from the specified release or unconsented-variance grounds
Every co-surety is released if one is released
options.explanation_md: The source gives a distinct co-surety rule.
